questions.question: What is the strong, hot and dry local wind that blows in the northern parts of the country in the months of May and June called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Loo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Loo is a robust, hot and dry local wind that blows in the northern parts of India, especially in the months of May and June.**
 
• It is also known as "loo winds" or **"loo storms".**
 
• These winds can cause heat strokes and dehydration in people.
 
• The word "loo" is derived from th**e Hindi word "loo," which means a hot wind.**
 
• Loo winds are caused by the intense heating of the Thar desert and the adjoining areas during summer.
 
• **Hence, the correct answer is option 3, Loo.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Mango showers, **mentioned in option 1, are pre-monsoon rains that occur in some parts of the country in the **months of May and June**.

 
 
• They are called so because they coincide with the ripening of mangoes.
 
 
 
• **Cherry blossoms**, mentioned in option 2, are unrelated to India's weather.
 
 
• They are a phenomenon that occurs in Japan and some other countries, where the cherry trees bloom in spring, usually in April.
 
 
 
• **Kalbaisakhi, **mentioned in option 4, is a local name for the Nor'westers, a type of thunderstorm that occurs in eastern India, e**specially in West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam, during the pre-monsoon season.**

questions.question: What do you call the distance between the centre of the nucleus and the outermost shell of an isolated atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Atomic size.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The distance between the center of the nucleus and the outermost shell of an isolated atom is called the atomic size.**

 
 
• Atomic size is determined by the number of shells or energy levels an atom has.
 
• The atomic size decreases from left to right across a period and increases from top to bottom down a group in the periodic table.
 
• The atomic size plays a crucial role in determining an element's chemical and physical properties.
 
 
 
• **Isotope** refers to the atoms of an element that have the** same number of protons but a different number of neutrons.**
 
• **Atomic mass** is the total number of protons and neutrons in the** nucleus of an atom**.

questions.question: Which article of Indian Constitution is related with the Conduct of business of the Government of a State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**166.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 4, i.e., Article 166 of the Indian Constitution, deals with the Conduct of Business of the Government of a State.**
 
• The article describes the procedure to be followed in the **State Legislature, including the conduct of proceedings, voting, and related matters.**
 
• The article also lays down the responsibilities of the** Governor, Chief Minister, and other Ministers in the State Government with respect to the conduct of business.**
 
• This article ensures that the State Government functions in a systematic and orderly manner and the interests of the citizens are protected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 132 **deals with the** Appellate Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court,** which means the power of the Supreme Court to hear appeals against the judgments of lower courts.
 
• ** Article 178** deals with the **Constitution of Legislatures in States, **which means the composition, powers, and functions of the State Legislatures.
 
• ** Article 144** deals with the** Enforcement of Orders and Decrees of Courts, **which means the duty of all authorities to enforce the orders and decrees of the courts within their jurisdiction.

questions.question: The price of one unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**nominal exchange rate.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The nominal exchange rate refers to the price of one unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency**.

 
 
• It is also known as the spot exchange rate and is the most commonly used exchange rate in international trade and finance.
 
 
 
• **A fixed exchange rate **refers to a system where a country's currency is pegged to another** currency or a basket of currencies, and the exchange rate remains constant.**
 
• **The real exchange rate, on the other hand, takes into account the inflation rates **of the two countries and measures the purchasing power of one currency in relation to another.
 
• ** Pegged float rate is a hybrid system where the exchange rate is allowed to float within a certain range, **but the central bank intervenes to keep it within the range.

questions.question: Which country has the longest written constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __ India.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** India's constitution is the longest in the world, with 448 articles and 12 schedules.**
 
• The constitution was adopted on **January 26, 1950, **and has since undergone several amendments.
 
• The constitution outlines the fundamental rights and duties of Indian citizens, as well as the structure and functions of the government.
 
• The constitution is considered a living document, as it has been amended over 100 times to reflect changing social, political, and economic conditions in India.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Option 2****: Indonesia's constitution has 37 chapters and 194 articles. It was adopted in 1945 and has been amended several times since then.**
 
• **Option 3****: Canada's constitution is not a single document, but rather a collection of laws, conventions, and court decisions. It includes the Constitution Act of 1867, the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, and other statutes and regulations.**
 
• **Option 4**: The United States of America's constitution has 7 articles and 27 amendments. It was adopted in 1787 and has since been amended several times. The Bill of Rights, which outlines individual rights and freedoms, is the first of 10 amendments to the Constitution.

questions.question: ______ is a kharif crop in north and rabi crop in south India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sesamum.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sesamum is a kharif crop in north India as it requires a hot and humid climate, while in south India, it is grown as a rabi crop as the weather conditions are suitable for its growth during winters.**
 
• ** Mustard is a rabi crop** mainly grown in northern and central parts of India during winter.
 
• **Castor is a kharif crop** mainly grown in the states of Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Rajasthan during the monsoon season.
 
• ** Linseed is also a rabi crop **mainly grown in the northern and central parts of India during the winter season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Sesamum, also known as sesame or til is widely used in Indian cuisine for its nutty flavor and high nutritional value. It is also used for making oil, sweets, and other food products.**
 
• Mustard is a rich omega-3 fatty acids, protein, and dietary fiber source. It is used for making mustard oil, pickles, and condiments.
 
• Castor is a medicinal plant; its oil is used for various purposes, such as treating skin problems, constipation, and arthritis. It is also used to manufacture soaps, lubricants, and plastics.
 
• Linseed is also known as flaxseed and is a rich source of omega-3 fatty acids, lignans, and dietary fiber. It is used for making oil, bread, and other food products. It is also used to manufacture textiles, paper, and paint.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The document referred to in the question is the Constitution of India.**
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad **signed the Constitution of India as th**e first President of India on November 26, 1949.**
 
• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India and provides the framework for governance and fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, formed in 1946 and included representatives from all parts of India.
 
• The Constitution of India came into effect on **January 26, 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day in India.**

• Option 4: **The Preamble to the Constitution of India is an introductory statement **that outlines the objectives and principles of the Constitution. The Constituent Assembly also adopted it along with the Constitution on November 26, 1949.

questions.question: Receipts of the government which create liability or reduce financial assets are termed as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capital receipts.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Capital receipts are the government's income that creates liability or reduces financial assets.**
 
• These receipts are generated from** sources **such as** borrowing, sale of assets, and recovery of loans.**
 
• Examples of capital receipts include proceeds from the sale of shares of** public sector undertakings, external borrowings, and recovery of loans.**
 
• Service agreements, on the other hand, are contracts between the government and other entities for the provision of services, and revenue receipts are generated from taxes, fees, and fines collected by the government.
 
• **Hence, the correct answer to the given question is option 2 - capital receipts.**

questions.question: As a country develops, it undergoes ‘structural changes'. Which of the following is a indicator of these structural changes?

options.text: The share of the industrial sector in GDP decreases
The share of agriculture in GDP declines
The share of agriculture in GDP increases
The share of agriculture in GDP becomes more than 50 percent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The share of agriculture in GDP declines.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Structural changes refer to the shift in the composition of an economy from one sector to another.
 
• The decline in the share of agriculture in **GDP is a common indicator of structural changes in a developing country.**
 
• This decline is usually accompanied by an increase in the share of the industrial and service sectors.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect as it suggests a decrease in the share of the industrial sector, which is not a typical indicator of structural changes.
 
• Option 4 is not a plausible scenario as it would mean that the country is heavily dependent on agriculture and has not diversified its economy.
 
• Option 3 is also incorrect as it contradicts the notion of structural changes and suggests that the country is moving towards a more agrarian economy.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which indicates that the country is undergoing structural changes as it shifts away from agriculture toward other sectors.

questions.question: Charaka is known as the father of ______.

• ** Charaka was an ancient Indian physician who lived around 300-200 BCE**.
 
• He is believed to have written the **Charaka Samhita, one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda,** which is still studied and used today.
 
• Ayurveda is a system of traditional medicine tha**t originated in India and is based **on the idea of balancing the body, mind, and spirit to promote health and prevent disease. It includes practices such as herbal medicine, massage, and yoga.
 
• Charaka's contributions to Ayurveda were significant.
 
• He is credited with developing the concept of the three doshas (vata, pitta, and Kapha), which are believed to govern the body's functions and need to be in balance for good health. He also emphasized preventive medicine and the importance of a healthy lifestyle.
 
• While Charaka is best known for his work in Ayurveda, the other options in question are also important cultural and artistic traditions in India.
